title: The Library That Keeps All Its Drafts

features.name: palimpsest shelves
features.desc-on-touch: stacked versions of the same book, each one a draft, each one absolutely final; you pull one out and the space it left fills with another version

features.name: variant pool
features.desc-on-touch: still water where every word-choice ever considered swims; you see the paragraph it could have been, the one it is, the one it will become

features.name: manuscript tower
features.desc-on-touch: pages stacked floor to ceiling, each one a different ending; if you look long enough they cascade into a story with no single telling

features.name: reading desk
features.desc-on-touch: a surface that holds four books at once, all of them the same story; your hand rests on whichever one you're currently becoming

features.name: textual archive
features.desc-on-touch: a directory of versions, each card showing a different word-count, publication date, and the name of whoever becomes the author by reading it

features.name: binding glyph
features.desc-on-touch: an inscription across all versions at once; you read it and each version says something different but equally true

inscription: here we keep every version a thing might have been, and let them whisper to each other in the dark

file.name: DraftArchive_TextualVariants_AllEditions.txt
file.note: every published version and forty-seven unpublished ones; the later drafts sometimes correct the earlier ones retroactively

exits.label: back toward the houses where all constructions happen at once
deeper into shelves where books have learned to write themselves
toward a reading chamber where every story remembers being told differently
